title: Hope comes home
hookLine: on the far shore, a waiting army hears a roar over the sea, and knows from the sound alone that Sita is found
carry: sundara kanda: the book where hope returns
last: SHED ANGER LIKE A SNAKE'S SKIN.

cards: On the northern shore, Angada, Jambavan and the whole search party have been waiting, watching the sea the way people watch the doors at an arrivals gate, trying to read a face before it reaches them. Then they hear it.
A roar, far off over the water, getting louder. Jambavan listens and says: that's the roar of someone who has succeeded.

teach.b: The flight back begins like the first one. Hanuman climbs a mountain on Lanka's shore, Arishta, and presses down to spring; Valmiki says the mountain sinks into the earth.
Then he's in the air, and Valmiki makes the sky an ocean: the moon a water lily, the sun a waterbird, the clouds its water weed. Nearing Mahendra, he roars, so the others will know before he lands.
They hear, and they know. The monkeys leap from tree to tree, waving branches, delirious. Hanuman lands among them, and they crowd around him with fruit and roots, cheering.
He bows to Jambavan and Angada and tells them in a few words: I've seen her. She's alive. Then, at Jambavan's urging, he tells them everything, from the beginning.
And that brings us near the end of the Sundara Kanda, the fifth book of the Ramayana. Sundara means beautiful, and teachers give different reasons for the name.

But ask Hindu families why they read it, and you'll often hear: it's the book of hope. It begins with Sita lost and a search party that nearly gave up. Its last chapters carry the news home over the sea: she's alive.
That's why many families read it aloud when someone is ill or in trouble, and finish the reading with prasad, sweets offered to God and shared.
Hope, in this book, isn't wishful thinking. It's a devoted servant who crossed the sea, and came back with the news.

how: Many Hindu families read the Sundara Kanda aloud in hard times or to fulfil a vow, often finishing with prasad shared around, and the return of Hanuman and the monkeys' joy on Mount Mahendra is read with delight.

games.q: a friend's family is going through a hard month, and they read the Sundara Kanda aloud each night. what is the book about?
o: Hanuman's journey: Sita found, and the news of hope brought home.
games.why: the Sundara Kanda follows Hanuman to Lanka and back, and its last chapters carry home the news that Sita is alive, which is why families turn to it for hope.

practice: If you pray, read a few lines of the Sundara Kanda or the Hanuman Chalisa for someone you love who's waiting on news, or simply say Hanuman's name for them.

If you don't pray, remember a time someone came home with good news, and the moment before the words when their face already told you. Breathe in that relief, and let the breath go out slowly, as if you were landing.

wordCard.voice: The return. Hanuman's leap back from Mount Arishta, his roar over the sea, and the search party who know, from the sound alone, that he has found Sita.

orig.note: Sanskrit ariṣṭa, the name of the mountain on Lanka's shore Hanuman leaps from.
